title: Warp Lane
summary: Race a kart through warp pipes: substitute u = g(x), move the limits into u-land and set the du factor so the kart exits on time.
subject: mathematics
ncertRef: Section 7.9, Evaluation of Definite Integrals by Substitution
concepts: Choosing u = g(x) where g′(x) sits in the integrand
du = g′(x) dx and the constant factor it brings
Changing the limits with the substitution
Limits that come out in reverse order
learningOutcome: The student can pick a substitution u = g(x) for a definite integral, find the factor from du = g′(x) dx, and change the limits, even when they come out reversed or negative.

levels.title: Into the warp
levels.adds: Baseline: with u = x² + 1, du = 2x dx; the limits x = a, b become u = g(a), g(b), and x dx = du/2 brings a factor 1/2 (Ex 7.2 Q1 to Q10; Ex 7.9).
hints: Pick u as the inside of the power or the root.
Put x = a and x = b into u = g(x) to get the new limits.
Compare du = g′(x) dx with what is left in the integrand to find the factor.

levels.title: Log and exp warps
levels.adds: New: u = log x turns dx/x into du, and u = 1 + eˣ turns eˣ dx into du (Ex 7.2; Ex 7.9 Q1 to Q8).
hints: If 1/x multiplies the rest, try u = log x.
log 1 = 0 and log e = 1, so the limits are often whole numbers.

levels.title: Backwards warp
levels.adds: New: u = cos x or u = 1 − x² decreases, so the new limits run backwards and du brings a minus sign (Ex 7.9; Ex 7.2).
hints: du = −sin x dx, so sin x dx = −du.
When x runs from 0 to π/2, cos x runs from 1 down to 0: keep that order.
Do not swap the limits without changing the sign.

levels.title: Warp master
levels.adds: Harder: factors of 1/3 from u = x³ + 1, and a negative limit from u = −x² (Ex 7.9 Q1 to Q8).
hints: du = 3x² dx, so x² dx = du/3.
Check the factor and both limits before you launch.

misconceptions: After a substitution the limits stay the same
The lower limit must always be the smaller number
du is just dx with a new name
